/audio/searchish/kokoro-heart/searchish-.speechText: stretchers. Definition: Informal: exaggerated stories or claims that go beyond the truth. In this passage, Huck calls the book’s exaggerations stretchers.
interest. Definition: Money earned by letting someone else use or invest your money. In this passage, Huck’s money earns interest every day.
dismal. Definition: Gloomy or depressing. In this passage, Huck finds the widow’s orderly life dismal.
indolently. Definition: Lazily, without making much effort. In this passage, the narrator indolently browses descriptions of diseases.
premonitory. Definition: Giving advance warning of something. In this passage, he treats premonitory symptoms as proof that he is ill.
invidious. Definition: Unfairly singling someone out, causing resentment. In this passage, he considers his one missing illness an invidious exclusion.
contemptuously. Definition: In a way that shows scorn or a lack of respect. In this passage, Humpty Dumpty smiles contemptuously at Alice’s confusion.
temper. Definition: A person’s usual disposition or tendency to become angry. In this passage, Humpty Dumpty imagines that verbs have a stubborn temper.
venture. Definition: Dare to do something that feels risky or uncertain. In this passage, Alice does not venture to ask about the words’ wages.
disquisitions. Definition: Detailed discussions or investigations of a subject. In this passage, the club consults books during its disquisitions.
scrivener. Definition: A person who professionally writes or prepares documents. In this passage, a scrivener puts Franklin’s proposals into formal wording.
charter. Definition: An official document granting rights to an organization. In this passage, the library company later obtains a charter.
frigate. Definition: A type of warship; here, a vehicle for an imagined journey. In this passage, a book carries the reader farther than a frigate.
traverse. Definition: A crossing or journey from one place to another. In this passage, even the poorest reader can take this traverse.
frugal. Definition: Economical; requiring little expense. In this passage, reading is a frugal way to travel in imagination.
precipitancy. Definition: Hasty action or judgment without enough care. In this passage, Descartes tries to avoid precipitancy in accepting a claim.
antecedence. Definition: The state of coming before something else. In this passage, he assigns an order even without natural antecedence.
enumerations. Definition: Complete, item-by-item lists or reviews. In this passage, he makes enumerations to check that nothing was omitted.
commodious. Definition: Spacious or roomy. In this passage, the speaker’s eyes occupy commodious caves beneath his forehead.
dictatorial. Definition: Insisting on obedience without allowing disagreement. In this passage, the speaker has a dictatorial voice.
obstinate. Definition: Stubbornly refusing to change. In this passage, even the speaker’s posture appears obstinate.
apparatus. Definition: Equipment designed for a particular purpose. In this passage, Vashti uses the lighting apparatus to darken her room.
dawdling. Definition: Moving or acting slowly and wasting time. In this passage, Vashti accuses Kuno of dawdling during the connection.
pneumatic. Definition: Operated by air pressure. In this passage, Vashti suggests sending the message by pneumatic post.
cavern. Definition: A large cave. In this passage, Huck and Jim keep their supplies in the cavern.
gust. Definition: A sudden, strong rush of wind. In this passage, a gust makes the tree branches toss about.
thrash. Definition: To move or strike about violently. In this passage, the rain would thrash along outside the cave.
disseminated. Definition: Spread or distributed widely. In this passage, native ads resemble the media in which they are disseminated.
induce. Definition: Persuade or lead someone to do something. In this passage, a misleading headline can induce someone to open an ad.
assessment. Definition: A careful evaluation or judgment. In this passage, the assessment considers the ad’s overall appearance.
